changes: Added an optional Sharpen slider below Brightness. Preview and saved photos use the same setting, which starts at 0% and leaves the white background unchanged.
Added HEIC and HEIF photo support when opening files, pasting copied files, and receiving photos from a phone.
Removed the preview instructions and privacy tagline. Kept the client version visible in the footer.
Added Receive from Phone. Scan a single-use QR code, choose a photo, and send it directly to IDFrame over a trusted local network.
Updated Fine hair to better separate hair from flag fragments beside the head in the tested portrait. Auto also uses the updated Fine hair weights when comparing removal modes.
Added Show in Folder after saving so you can find the finished photo in File Explorer.
The Save dialog remembers the folder from your last successful export, even after restarting IDFrame.
Switching removal modes now preserves the current gradient animation and idle countdown while the photo reprocesses.
Added distinct processing gradients for pasting photos, removing backgrounds, and saving photos in Light and Dark modes.
Made gradient bursts brighter and wider in Light and Dark modes. Bursts now start at random locations across the workspace.
Made gradient bursts easier to see near the header in Light and Dark modes, with randomized colors and positions every 10 seconds while idle.
Added gradient feedback for workspace interactions and while processing photos. Longer jobs repeat the effect every 5 seconds.
Added head-and-shoulders, eye-level, headroom and centerline guides to the photo preview. Toggle Guides or drag the right-edge dots to adjust eye level and headroom without changing photo pixels.
Added a silhouette over the live camera feed, with PRC/LERIS photo reminders. Guides adapt to the selected photo size and are positioning aids rather than a compliance check.

Camera capture now opens a clean still review with Use Photo, Retake and Cancel. Capture releases the camera; Retake reopens it. Guide graphics and dimming are excluded from captured and saved photos.

Added occasional soft mesh-gradient blooms to the existing app background, with blue, cyan, violet and warm gold colors tuned for Light and Dark modes. The layout, controls, photo previews and saved-photo backgrounds are preserved.
Blooms gently drift and fade for 3–5 seconds, with randomized 8–15 second idle gaps. Animation pauses during processing and stops while hidden or minimized to keep the workspace responsive.

Added a Camera button with a live viewfinder and device selector for built-in and USB cameras recognized by Windows. Capture loads the photo into the existing editing workflow; Cancel keeps the previous photo.

Camera selection follows device identities rather than fixed camera numbers, refreshes when devices connect or disconnect, and remembers the selected device during the app session. Devices are released on capture, cancellation and switching.
Included Qt Multimedia support for camera capture in the updated client runtime. Photos stay local; capture uses the camera stream resolution rather than a screenshot of the preview.
Added a Photo size selector: 2×2 inches (default), 1×1 inch, and Philippine passport 35×45 mm. All formats retain white backgrounds and 600 DPI PNG exports.

Preview proportions, save labels and person-based filenames follow the selected size. Outputs are 1200×1200, 600×600 and 827×1063 pixels respectively. Size changes preserve framing, rotation, brightness and cleanup edits.
Expanded manual rotation to −180° through +180° for sideways and upside-down photos, retaining precise 0.1° adjustments.

Added a best-effort Auto-skew button to estimate eye-level rotation offline when clicked. Review the result and fine-tune Rotation as needed; uncertain detections leave the angle unchanged. Framing, brightness and cleanup edits are preserved.
Arranged the top row as Open Photo, Paste Ctrl+V, Auto-skew and Edit, with distinct blue, teal, gold and purple buttons for easier identification in Light and Dark modes.
Added a Rotation slider beside Zoom to straighten tilted portraits manually from −30° to +30°, with 0.1° adjustments and a horizontal preview guide. The guide is not printed.

Saved photos include the selected rotation with the existing white 2×2 inch, 1200×1200 pixel, 600 DPI format. Rotation preserves cleanup edits and brightness; Reset Adjustments and opening another photo clear the angle.

Updated IDFrame branding to the blue-and-gold Clean Cut portrait logo across the application, update dialog, and installed desktop and taskbar shortcuts. Added multiple icon sizes for clear Windows display.
Updated changelog terminology to describe background removal as processing logic. Application behavior is unchanged.

Added a Restore brush in Edit to paint back original photo pixels, including parts removed by the background-removal logic. Switch between Erase and Restore with a shared brush size and Undo/Redo history.
Applying edits preserves crop and brightness. Source photos and the current processing logic remain unchanged. Restore may reveal the original background in painted areas.
Removed the experimental Test P3M comparison feature at the host's request. The existing removal modes, PySide6 workspace and cleanup editor remain available.
Existing production models and locally saved training candidates are preserved. No installer was rebuilt and no OTA update was published.

Moved the main workspace to PySide6 with resizable windows, rounded Light/Dark controls and cached previews. Loading, background removal, preview preparation and saving run outside the interface thread.

Added a separate Edit portrait window to erase unwanted residue, adjust eraser size, zoom and pan, and undo or redo strokes. Apply keeps the edits; Cancel preserves the previous result. Crop and brightness are retained when edits are applied.
Kept white 2×2 inch, 1200×1200 pixel / 600 DPI PNG exports, safe person-based naming, clipboard paste and visible removal-mode choices. Improved window sizing for small or scaled displays.
Prepared the complete Qt runtime for the existing signed LAN updater. Publication remains controlled by the host; installed clients keep working offline.
Introduced the combined modern workspace with side-by-side Original and 2×2 Preview cards, a right editing panel, rounded buttons and cards, and three visible removal-mode radio choices.

Added instant Light and Dark appearance switching with a remembered per-user preference. Changing appearance preserves the current photo, crop, brightness, and processing state; exported backgrounds remain white.
Styled the offline changelog and person-name prompt in both themes. Smaller windows retain the save action and status while editing controls scroll when needed.
Added a live Brightness slider before saving: below 100% darkens the portrait and above 100% lightens it. The saved photo uses the selected brightness while its background stays white.
Reset and opening a new photo restore neutral brightness. Adjusting brightness does not rerun background removal or modify the original file.

Fixed the shortcut rename notification that could leave an undeletable Portrait Studio ghost icon in Windows Explorer. Pinned taskbar shortcut filenames are preserved, and unrelated existing shortcuts are not overwritten.
Refactored window setup, model preprocessing, release payload assembly, and update staging into smaller documented functions while preserving existing workflows.
Added purpose docstrings throughout maintained application, deployment, training, and test code, along with consistent formatting and a contributor code map.
Added development-only formatting, lint, and function-documentation checks. Photo dimensions, removal models, naming rules, and LAN update compatibility remain unchanged.
Renamed Portrait Studio to IDFrame in the application, changelog, and update messages.
Existing installed shortcuts are renamed to IDFrame when the destination name is unused, retaining the camera icon and compatible update paths.
Project source is now maintained on GitHub. LAN OTA publication remains controlled by the host.
Saving now asks for the person's name and generates PersonName_2x2.png, using underscores for spaces.
Duplicate filenames receive numbered suffixes such as _002 and _003. Existing photos are preserved, including when another save creates the same filename at the same time.
The name prompt shows the generated filename, validates Windows filename characters, and clears the person's name when a new photo is opened or pasted.
The host can follow its active LAN IPv4 address automatically when starting the server or preparing a release, and checks for changes every three seconds while the server runs.
The host's own registered application follows that same LAN IP instead of localhost. Remote client addresses are not rewritten.
Updated the host firewall setup script to retain local-subnet access when the host IP changes.
Added Auto as the default removal mode. It compares both local model results for missing person interiors and background spill, then selects one complete result.
Shows whether Auto selected Protect person or Fine hair. Both manual modes remain available if you prefer the other result.
Auto can take longer because it evaluates both models. Selection is a heuristic and can still make mistakes; an available result is retained if one model cannot detect a person.
Added Protect person as the default removal mode after testing the original client portraits with missing hair and scalp areas.
Kept Fine hair as a selectable mode for detailed curls. Switching modes after processing recomputes the result and resets its crop.
Replaced the experimental two-model blend with separate modes to avoid adding patches or damaging the head outline. Both modes remain offline.
Prepared an experimental two-model protection pass against the client screen-photo examples.
Testing the original portraits exposed artifacts; this approach was replaced by the selectable modes in v1.1.8.
Added an interactive 2 × 2 crop preview with a zoom slider, mouse-wheel zoom, and drag-to-position controls.
Reset restores the full photo framing. Opening or pasting a new photo clears the previous crop.
Saved photos use the selected framing, rendered from the full-resolution cutout, with a white background at 1200 × 1200 pixels and 600 DPI.
Added a Changelog button beside the application heading.
Browse release notes by version, with your installed version selected automatically. Notes are available offline.
Added a centered Checking Updates dialog with the camera logo and download progress, without a console window.
Existing clients can receive launcher improvements through OTA. The refreshed launcher takes effect after closing and reopening the updated app.

Adapted the portrait model using the camo and low-quality photo folders, retaining earlier curl examples. Some missing faces and clothing are better preserved; severe camouflage and blurry boundaries remain imperfect.
Added a locally adapted MODNet portrait matting model for finer hair and curls.
Preserved continuous hair opacity and used higher-resolution, proportionally resized model inputs.
Kept the original U2Net model as a fallback when the matting model is absent.
Changed exports to 2 × 2 inches: 1200 × 1200 pixels at 600 DPI, with a solid white background.
Fit portraits proportionally into the square while preserving original files.
Prepared Philippine passport photo dimensions of 35 × 45 mm at 600 DPI; later replaced by the 2 × 2 inch format in v1.1.2.
Displayed the client version in the application title and heading, with automatic version increments for changed releases.
Included camera-logo branding and refresh support for desktop, Start menu, and existing taskbar shortcuts.
Included clipboard photo pasting with Ctrl+V alongside Open photo.
Included 600 DPI export with the earlier 208 × 208 pixel dimensions.
Updated the default LAN update port to 8766 and provided an installer upgrade for version 1 clients.
Initial offline Python portrait background remover with white-background PNG exports.
Added a Windows installer, desktop shortcut, and startup checks for LAN updates.
Downloaded only changed application files while retaining unchanged files.
